record.paper_title: Jaynes–Cummings Model and a Non–Commutative “Geometry” : A Few Problems Noted
record.original_question: Can the classical Hopf bundles over the real numbers, complex numbers, quaternions, and octonions be generalized to non-commutative versions in a way that is mathematically or physically meaningful, given that local descriptions of the classical Hopf bundles encounter singular lines called Dirac strings?

evidence.quote: The Hopf bundles (which are famous examples of fiber bundles) over K = R, C, H (the field of quaternion numbers), O (the field of octanion numbers) are classical objects and they are never written down in a local manner. If we write them locally then we are forced to encounter singular lines called the Dirac strings, see [1].

We would like to make the Hopf bundles non–commutative. Whether such a generalization is meaningful or not is not clear at the current time, however it may be worth trying, see for example [5] or more recently [6] and its references.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
The classical Hopf fibrations are the principal bundles
\[ S^0 \hookrightarrow S^1 \to S^1, \qquad S^1 \hookrightarrow S^3 \to S^2, \qquad S^3 \hookrightarrow S^7 \to S^4, \qquad S^7 \hookrightarrow S^{15} \to S^8, \]
arising respectively from the normed division algebras $\mathbb{R}$, $\mathbb{C}$, $\mathbb{H}$ (quaternions), and $\mathbb{O}$ (octonions), via the maps $(x,y)\mapsto xy^{-1}$ defined on pairs of elements of the relevant algebra. These bundles are nontrivial: any attempt to describe them by a single global section / local trivialization produces coordinate singularities along curves (Dirac strings).

A noncommutative principal bundle (in the sense of Hopf–Galois extensions or quantum principal bundles) consists of a (typically noncommutative) $*$-algebra $A$ playing the role of "functions on the total space", a Hopf algebra $H$ coacting on $A$, and a base subalgebra $B = A^{co H}$ of coinvariants, such that the canonical map $A \otimes_B A \to A \otimes H$ is bijective. The classical Hopf bundles are recovered when $A$, $H$, and $B$ are commutative algebras of functions on the corresponding spheres.

Problem. Construct, for each $\mathbb{K} \in \{\mathbb{R}, \mathbb{C}, \mathbb{H}, \mathbb{O}\}$, a noncommutative deformation of the classical Hopf bundle over $\mathbb{K}$, i.e. a Hopf–Galois extension $B \subset A$ with structure Hopf algebra $H$ that specializes in a suitable classical limit to the corresponding Hopf fibration, and demonstrate that the construction is mathematically meaningful (e.g. yields nontrivial $K$-theoretic invariants, projective modules realizing nontrivial "noncommutative line/quaternionic/octonionic bundles", or admits a connection with nonzero curvature) or physically meaningful (e.g. provides a noncommutative analogue of the Dirac monopole, instanton, or related gauge-theoretic structure). In particular, decide whether such generalizations exist in the octonionic case $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{O}$, where nonassociativity obstructs the standard Hopf-algebraic framework.
artifact.status_search_result: Noncommutative Hopf fibrations have been constructed in the complex case (e.g. the Hopf fibration of the Podleś quantum sphere as a quantum principal $U(1)$-bundle by Brzeziński–Majid, and quantum $SU(2)\to S^4_q$ instanton bundles by Landi and collaborators), giving partial positive answers for $\mathbb{C}$ and $\mathbb{H}$. The octonionic case, due to nonassociativity, is much less developed and requires quasi-Hopf or nonassociative frameworks; no widely-accepted complete construction is known. Overall the broad question of a uniform and "physically meaningful" noncommutative generalization across $\mathbb{R},\mathbb{C},\mathbb{H},\mathbb{O}$ remains open.

status_evidence.title: Quantum group gauge theory on quantum spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Brzeziński and Majid constructed quantum principal bundles including the q-deformed Hopf fibration of the Podleś sphere.
status_evidence.claim: Noncommutative version of the complex Hopf bundle exists.

status_evidence.title: Noncommutative instantons on the 4-sphere from quantum groups
status_evidence.snippet: Landi et al. construct noncommutative SU(2) Hopf bundle over a quantum 4-sphere.
status_evidence.claim: Quaternionic Hopf bundle admits noncommutative deformations.
